ja: この薬は眠くなるか、伺いたいのですが。
en: I was wondering if this medicine makes you drowsy.
alternatives: I was wondering whether this medicine causes drowsiness.
Could you tell me whether this medicine causes drowsiness?
point: was wondering で丁寧に。中身は if 節

ja: 薬の服用中、お酒は控えるべきですか？
en: Should I avoid alcohol on this medicine?
alternatives: Should I avoid drinking while taking this medicine?
Must I avoid alcohol with this medicine?
point: avoid の後ろは名詞か動名詞で、to 不定詞は使えない

ja: 心配なのは頭痛じゃなく、毎朝のめまいなんです。
en: What worries me isn't the headache, it's the morning dizziness.
alternatives: It's not the headache that worries me, it's the morning dizziness.
It's the dizziness every morning that worries me, not the headache.
point: 「心配なのは〜」は What worries me is で強調する

ja: かかりつけ医が週末も診てくれたらいいのに。
en: I wish our family doctor saw patients on weekends.
alternatives: If only our family doctor were open on weekends.
I wish our family doctor worked weekends.
point: 今の願望は wish + 過去形

ja: 左耳がおかしいので、今日診ていただけないでしょうか？
en: I was wondering if someone could check my left ear today.
alternatives: Is there any chance someone could look at my left ear today?
Could someone possibly take a look at my left ear today?
point: 「〜でしょうか」は I was wondering if で柔らかく

ja: 熱があるなら、休んでね。
en: Rest if you have a fever.
alternatives: If you have a fever, rest.
Rest if you've got a fever.
point: 「熱がある」は have a fever、a を忘れずに

ja: 息子は熱が出ただけじゃなく、吐きもしたんです。
en: Not only did my son have a fever, he vomited.
alternatives: My son not only had a fever, he also threw up.
My son didn't just have a fever, he threw up too.
point: Not only が文頭なら did my son have の語順

ja: 近くに薬局はありますか？
en: Is there a pharmacy near here?
alternatives: Is there a drugstore nearby?
Is there a pharmacy nearby?
point: 「ありますか」は Is there ～? で聞く

ja: 薬を飲んで3日、頭痛が前よりひどい気がします。
en: Three days on this medicine, my headaches feel worse.
alternatives: It's been three days, and my headaches feel worse.
I've taken it for three days, but my headache's worse.
point: 「前よりひどい」は worse で言える

ja: 薬剤師さんによると、胃薬は抗生物質を弱めるかも。
en: The pharmacist said my stomach medicine might weaken the antibiotics.
alternatives: According to the pharmacist, my stomach pills could weaken the antibiotics.
The pharmacist told me my stomach medicine might weaken the antibiotics.
point: said の後は時制を一つ下げて might にする

ja: 昨日ジムでやりすぎたのかもしれません。
en: I might have overdone it at the gym yesterday.
alternatives: Maybe I pushed myself too hard at the gym yesterday.
Maybe I overdid it at the gym yesterday.
point: 過去の推量は might + have + 過去分詞

ja: この薬で副作用が出たことはありますか？
en: Have you ever had side effects from this?
alternatives: Has this medicine ever given you side effects?
Did this ever give you side effects?
point: 経験を聞くので Have you ever had、「〜で」は from

ja: 先生、手術は必要かどうか知りたいです。
en: I want to know if surgery's necessary.
alternatives: I'd like to know whether I need surgery.
I want to know whether I need an operation.
point: 「〜かどうか」は if / whether で、語順は平叙文のまま

ja: 2日前からずっと咳が止まらないんです。
en: I've been coughing nonstop for two days.
alternatives: I've been coughing for two days straight.
My cough hasn't stopped in two days.
point: 今も続いている症状は I've been ＋ -ing ＋ for で言う

ja: 先生にアレルギーを伝えておけばよかった。
en: I wish I'd told the doctor about my allergy.
alternatives: If only I'd mentioned my allergy to the doctor.
I should have told the doctor about my allergy.
point: 過去の後悔は I wish の後を過去完了にする

ja: 先生、咳が出るんです。
en: I have a cough.
alternatives: I've got a cough.
Doctor, I have a cough.
point: 咳は a cough と数えられる名詞で表す

ja: 彼、健診を受けてたら今ごろ入院してないのに。
en: If he'd had a checkup, he wouldn't be hospitalized now.
alternatives: Had he gotten a checkup, he wouldn't be hospitalized now.
If he'd been checked, he wouldn't be hospitalized now.
point: 過去の仮定は had+過去分詞、今の結果は wouldn't be

ja: 着いた頃には、もう熱は下がっていました。
en: My fever had gone down when I arrived.
alternatives: My fever had already broken when I arrived.
When I arrived, my fever had already gone.
point: 着いた時点より前に下がったので had gone down と過去完了

ja: 夫には明日、絶対に検査を受けさせます。
en: I'm definitely making my husband get checked out tomorrow.
alternatives: I'll definitely make my husband get checked out tomorrow.
I'm definitely getting my husband checked out tomorrow.
point: 嫌がる相手に無理にさせるのは make 人 do。「診てもらう」は get checked out

ja: 先生に、薬の後は一日安静って言われた。
en: The doctor said to rest for a day.
alternatives: My doctor said I should rest for a day.
The doctor told me to rest for a day.
point: 指示を伝えるときは told me to ＋ 動詞の原形

ja: 今日会議がなければ、病院に行くのに。
en: If I had no meeting, I'd see a doctor.
alternatives: If I didn't have a meeting, I'd see a doctor.
I'd see a doctor if I didn't have this meeting.
point: 今の事実に反する仮定は If + 過去形、I'd 〜

ja: 先生に、昨日の牡蠣が原因かもと言われました。
en: The doctor said the oysters might've made me sick.
alternatives: The doctor told me the oysters might've made me sick.
According to the doctor, the oysters might've made me sick.
point: 過去の推量は might have + 過去分詞

ja: 母が転んで、手首を押さえたまま動けなかった。
en: My mom fell and couldn't move, holding her wrist.
alternatives: My mother fell and couldn't move, clutching her wrist.
Mom fell and was stuck there, gripping her wrist.
point: 「押さえたまま」は文末に holding を添える

ja: 薬剤師さんが気づかなければ、妻は入院してたかも。
en: If the pharmacist hadn't noticed, my wife might've been hospitalized.
alternatives: Had the pharmacist not noticed, my wife might've been hospitalized.
My wife could've been hospitalized if the pharmacist hadn't noticed.
point: 過去の事実の反対は If 〜 hadn't noticed、結果は might've been

ja: 妹は熱があるのに、試験を受けると言い張ってる。
en: Despite her fever, she insists on taking the exam.
alternatives: My sister insists on taking the exam despite her fever.
My sister's sick, but she insists on taking the exam.
point: insist は on + 動名詞、「のに」は Despite で前に出す

ja: 教えてくれた花粉症の薬、まだありますか？
en: Do you still have the allergy medicine you mentioned?
alternatives: Is the allergy medicine you told me about still available?
Have you still got the allergy medicine you mentioned?
Is the allergy medicine you recommended still in stock?
point: medicine の直後に you mentioned をつなげる。関係詞 that は省略できる

ja: ほかの薬は飲んでいますか？
en: Are you taking any other medicine?
alternatives: Are you on any other medicine?
Are you taking any other medication?
point: 薬を「飲む」は drink ではなく take

ja: 痛みがなくても、抗生物質は飲み切るべきですか？
en: Even if I'm pain-free, should I finish the antibiotics?
alternatives: Should I finish the antibiotics even if it doesn't hurt?
Even if the pain's gone, should I finish the antibiotics?
point: 「〜ても」は even if、条件節は現在形

ja: この薬、処方薬と飲んでも大丈夫ですか？
en: Can I take this with my prescription?
alternatives: May I take this with my prescription?
Is this okay to take with my prescription?
point: 「処方薬」は my prescription と短く言える

ja: 熱が出て、昨夜は眠れなかった。
en: I couldn't sleep with a fever.
alternatives: A fever kept me up all night.
I had a fever and couldn't sleep.
point: 「眠れなかった」は couldn't sleep で表す

ja: 食後の薬ですが、朝食を抜いた日も飲むべきですか？
en: Should I still take this if I skip breakfast?
alternatives: Do I still need to take this if I skip breakfast?
If I skip breakfast, should I take this anyway?
point: 「〜も」は still、if 節は現在形

ja: 一晩高熱が続き、彼女は朝一番に受診しました。
en: Feverish all night, she saw a doctor first thing.
alternatives: Having run a fever all night, she saw a doctor.
After a feverish night, she saw a doctor first thing.
point: 理由は文頭の分詞や形容詞で先に置ける

ja: この薬を飲んでから、発疹が出てきたんです。
en: I've broken out in a rash since taking this.
alternatives: Since I started taking this, I've broken out in a rash.
I've come out in a rash since I started this medicine.
point: 発疹が出るは break out in a rash、since と現在完了

ja: 兄は今日、病院で診てもらうんだ。
en: My brother is seeing a doctor today.
alternatives: My brother has a doctor's appointment today.
My brother's going to the doctor today.
point: 決まった予定は進行形 is seeing で表せる
